issues.reason: Measures & units itself licenses a dimension noun that appears in no word of the sentence — "costs $20" is stored under the scale `price` — so supplying `value` for an index's percentage rise is the same licensed move, and the atom is true, well-typed and asserts no more than "increased 3.3 percent".

gaps_confirmed: extent-of-change stated as a percentage on a change verb ('increased 3.3 percent') — Measure presumes a stated scale and a physical unit, while (Fraction n 100) is reserved for partitive proportions of a definite set, so no licensed form fits squarely
new_gaps: `percent` as a unit — the unit slot is defined over lemmatized physical units with canonical-unit conversion factors, and a dimensionless ratio unit has no place in that lexicon

a light verb as the comparative's verb ('the index did better than …') — the adverbial-comparative rule reifies two events of the surface verb, but a semantically empty `do` class atom carries no content and nothing addresses reconstructing the elided predicate
notes: The Measure rides the increase EVENT, not the index, which is the correct attachment (an index is not 3.3 percent); the reviewer's own registered gap plus the calibration line make this acceptable improvisation. The rest of the parse — two reified `do` events joined by (More good …), the name/kind split on 'Standard & Poor's 500', Patient for the intransitive change-of-state subject — is textbook.
